Actual Article Body:
Posted By: David Bell
September 29, 2026

SAFFORD — Gila Valley Indivisible is conducting two events to help increase voter turnout.

As part of the No Kings Vote Early events happening across the nation on Oct. 17, Gila Valley Indivisible will conduct an auto parade that will start at the Firth Park parking lot at 9 a.m. and end back at the park at 10 a.m.

Immediately thereafter, participants will gather at the park with signs to rally encouragement for early voting. The rally will run from 10 a.m. to noon.

Mail-in voters are encouraged to bring their completed ballot and drop it in the Graham County Elections drop box in the parking lot behind the General Services Building, across the street from Firth Park.

In announcing the events, Gila Valley Indivisible describes the effort as “aimed at driving historic early voter turnout.” Both Gila Valley Indivisible and No Kings describe themselves as nonpartisan organizations.

Auto parades followed by rallies have previously occurred in Graham County. Turning Point USA and local conservatives conducted multiple “Trump Trains” in support of Donald Trump’s effort to win election to the presidency in 2024.

The deadline to register and be eligible to vote in the Nov. 3 General Election is Oct. 5. Early voting begins Oct. 7.
